propositions.text: Appellant alleges Somali citizenship and appeals RPD's refugee claim rejection
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX (a.k.a. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, the Appellant, alleges he is a citizen of Somalia and appeals a decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) rejecting his claim for refugee protection.

propositions.text: Appellant asks RAD to set aside RPD decision and find him a Convention refugee or person in need of protection
propositions.quote: The Appellant asks that the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) set aside the decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) and substitute a decision with its own determination that the Appellant is a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection.

propositions.text: Alternatively, Appellant requests RAD to refer matter back to RPD with a differently constituted panel
propositions.quote: In the alternative, the Appellant requests that the RAD refer the matter back to the RPD with a differently constituted panel.

propositions.text: Appellant submitted new evidence under s.110(4) IRPA and requests oral hearing under s.110(6) IRPA
propositions.quote: The Appellant has submitted new evidence with the appeal as referred to in s.110(4) of the IRPA1 and requests an oral hearing be held pursuant to s.110(6) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant alleges Somali citizenship, appeals RPD rejection, requests RAD to set aside or refer back, submits new evidence, and requests oral hearing.

propositions.text: RAD confirms RPD's determination and dismisses the appeal under s.111(1)(a) IRPA
propositions.quote: Pursuant to ss. 111(1)(a) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA), the RAD confirms the determination of the RPD and dismisses the appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD confirms the RPD decision and dismisses the appeal under IRPA s.111(1)(a).

propositions.text: Appellant born in Qoryoley, Somalia, minority clan family, father shot by Al-Shabab in 2009
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleged before the RPD that he was born in Qoryoley, Somalia on XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, into a family from the minority XXXX clan. On XXXX XXXX, 2009, Al-Shabab came to the family farm to collect produce. They told the Appellant's father that they need young boys to join their fight. The Appellant's father told them he was a Sufi and a peace lover. Al-Shabab became upset and shot the Appellant's father.

propositions.text: Al-Shabab asked Appellant's mother about him; she said he was not home
propositions.quote: They then asked the Appellant's mother where the Appellant was. She told them he was not at home.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant alleges he was born in Somalia, father was shot by Al-Shabab, and mother said appellant was not home.

propositions.text: Appellant hid at uncle's home, fled to Ethiopia Dec 2009, stayed until April 2011, then South Africa, then Brazil, Panama, Mexico, US asylum claim Feb 2013
propositions.quote: The Appellant went into hiding at his uncle's home and he travelled to Addis Ababa, Ethiopia arriving on December 20, 2009. The Appellant remained in Ethiopia until April 1, 2011, when he departed for South Africa. He remained in South Africa for four months and then managed to fly to Brazil. He then travelled through numerous countries including Brazil, Panama and Mexico. He arrived in the United States (US), on February 22, 2013 and made an asylum claim at the border.

propositions.text: Appellant's US lawyer advised asylum claim likely denied and to go to Canada
propositions.quote: On June 10, 2014, the Appellant met with his lawyer who told him his asylum claim would likely be denied. The lawyer advised the Appellant to go to Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant fled Somalia through several countries, claimed asylum in US, was advised to go to Canada.

propositions.text: Appellant crossed illegally into Canada June 29, 2014, detained, claimed refugee Oct 9, 2014
propositions.quote: The Appellant crossed the border illegally on June 29, 2014. He was detained in Manitoba and subsequently made a refugee claim on October 9, 2014.

propositions.text: RPD rejected claim Feb 23, 2015, found appellant not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection, identity and credibility issues
propositions.quote: In a decision of February 23, 2015, the RPD rejected the claim, finding that the Appellant was neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection. The RPD further found that the Appellant had not established his identity and his credibility was seriously undermined by his testimony.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant crossed illegally, claimed refugee, and the RPD rejected claim citing identity and credibility issues.

propositions.text: Appellant submits RPD erred in identity and credibility findings
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits the following issues: a) The RPD erred in its identity findings b) The RPD erred in its credibility findings

paragraphs.summary: The appellant submits the RPD erred in identity and credibility findings.

propositions.text: RAD must proceed without hearing on RPD record but may accept new documentary evidence and submissions
propositions.quote: As provided for in s. 110(3) of IRPA, with certain exceptions, the RAD must proceed without a hearing, on the basis of the record of the proceedings of the RPD and may accept documentary evidence and written submissions from the Minister and refugee claimant.

propositions.text: Under s.110(4) IRPA, appellant may present only evidence arising after rejection or not reasonably available or not reasonably expected to be presented before rejection
propositions.quote: Subsection 110(4) of IRPA provides that the person who is the subject of the appeal may present only evidence that arose after the rejection of their claim or that was not reasonably available, or that the person could not reasonably have been expected in the circumstances to present, at the time of the rejection.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD must proceed without hearing on RPD record but may accept new evidence only if it arose after rejection or was not reasonably available or expected before rejection.

propositions.text: Appellant tendered four new evidence documents: affidavit, teacher's letter, marriage certificate, friend's letter
propositions.quote: The Appellant has tendered four documents as proposed new evidence in support of his appeal: a) An affidavit from XXXX XXXX XXXX2 dated April 9, 2015 b) A letter from a former teacher, XXXX XXXX XXXX,3 dated March 25, 2015 c) A copy of a Marriage Certificate4 d) A letter from XXXX XXXX,5 a friend in South Africa.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant submitted four new documents as evidence: affidavit, teacher's letter, marriage certificate, and friend's letter.

propositions.text: RAD considers if evidence arose after rejection, can prove current or post-rejection events, and timing of event or document
propositions.quote: Firstly, did the evidence arise after the rejection of the Appellant's refugee claim? * The RAD may consider whether the evidence is capable of proving the current state of affairs in the country of feared persecution, or an event that occurred or a circumstance that arose after the rejection of the refugee claim * The RAD will consider not only the date on which the document came into existence but the timing of the event or circumstance which the document seeks to prove.

propositions.text: Section 110(4) contemplates evidence arising after rejection, not after hearing but before rejection
propositions.quote: It is important to note here that Section 110(4) does not contemplate whether the evidence arose after the RPD's hearing but rather after the rejection of the Appellant's claim.

propositions.text: If evidence arose after hearing but before rejection, RAD considers if it could have been presented by post-hearing submission
propositions.quote: Where a document arose after the hearing but before the rejection of the refugee claim, it is necessary for the RAD to consider whether the Appellant could have presented the document to the RPD by way of a post-hearing submission.

propositions.text: If evidence did not arise after rejection, RAD considers if it was reasonably available or unknown at hearing
propositions.quote: Secondly, if the RAD finds that the evidence did not arise after the rejection of the Appellant's refugee claim, it must consider the next factor in Section 110(4). * If the evidence is capable of proving only an event that occurred or circumstances that arose prior to the rejection, has the Appellant established that the evidence was not reasonably available for presentation to the RPD before it rejected the claim, or that it proves a fact that was unknown to him at the time of the hearing?

propositions.text: If evidence was reasonably available, RAD considers if appellant could reasonably have been expected to present it before rejection
propositions.quote: Thirdly, if the RAD finds that the evidence did not arise after the rejection of the Appellant's refugee claim and that it was reasonably available at the time of the rejection, it must consider the final part of the Section 110(4) test: * Could the Appellant reasonably have been expected in the circumstances to have presented the evidence prior to the rejection of his refugee claim? If so, the evidence need not be considered.

propositions.text: If appellant could not reasonably have been expected to present evidence before rejection, RAD assesses credibility, relevance and materiality
propositions.quote: If the Appellant could not reasonably have been expected to present the evidence to the RPD, the RAD will proceed to assess the credibility, relevance and materiality of the document.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD explains the s.110(4) test for admitting new evidence based on timing, availability, and reasonableness of presentation before rejection.

propositions.text: Appellant submits he was unaware of insufficient identity evidence
propositions.quote: In the case at hand, the Appellant submits he was unaware he had not provided sufficient evidence to establish his identity.

propositions.text: RAD accepts appellant's explanation and admits new evidence under s.110(4) despite availability before rejection
propositions.quote: The RAD finds that as much as these documents should have been available prior to the rejection of the Appellant's claim, the RAD accepts the Appellant's explanation that he would be unaware of the need to supply additional identity documentation. The RAD will admit the evidence under the requirements of s. 110(4).

paragraphs.summary: The appellant says he was unaware of insufficient identity evidence; the RAD accepts this and admits the new evidence under s.110(4).

propositions.text: Affidavit states affiant met appellant in Somalia in 2007 and 2008, appellant participated in Sufi customs, name indicates Ashraf clan
propositions.quote: The Appellant submitted an affidavit6 from an individual who states that he met the Appellant in Qoryoley in 2007, while he was visiting his uncle. He further states that he encountered the Appellant in Mogadishu at a market in 2008. The Affiant submits the Appellant participated in Sufi customs and prayers at the mosque, he is "certain XXXX XXXX XXXX". He also states the name "XXXX" is given to members of the Ashraf clan and this is another reason to confirm his identity.

paragraphs.summary: The affidavit states the affiant met the appellant in Somalia, observed Sufi customs, and notes the appellant's clan name.

propositions.text: Affidavit's identity statements rely on appellant's self-reported information and actions
propositions.quote: The RAD has reviewed the affidavit and notes the affiant is basing his identity statements on self-reported information provided by the Appellant. The Appellant's name, family information, clan identity and religious practices are all founded in information and actions of the Appellant.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the affidavit's identity statements rely on the appellant's self-reported information and actions.

propositions.text: Affiant's information about appellant's father's death is from unconfirmed, unverifiable source
propositions.quote: The Affiant further relates that he learned about the death and the circumstances surrounding the death of the Appellant's father from an unidentified female trader in Somalia. The RAD finds this information is derived from an unconfirmed report obtained from a source which cannot be verified or confirmed.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the affidavit's information about the appellant's father's death is from an unconfirmed, unverifiable source.

propositions.text: RPD accepted appellant was individual last in Somalia in 2009
propositions.quote: The RAD notes in assessing the content of the affidavit that the RPD in its Reasons has accepted that the Appellant was the individual XXXX XXXX , who was last present in Somalia in 2009.

propositions.text: Affidavit does not confirm appellant's Somali nationality; appellant could be Somali heritage born elsewhere
propositions.quote: The RAD finds the affidavit submitted does not allow the affiant to confirm the Appellant's identity as a national of Somalia. The RAD notes the Appellant could also be the child of one or both parents who were of Somali heritage, but born and raised elsewhere.

propositions.text: Affidavit shows appellant speaks Somali, appears Ashraf clan member, but provides no additional evidence confirming Somali nationality
propositions.quote: The RAD finds as much as the affiant states that the Appellant speaks the Somali language, has the appearance and actions of a member of the Ashraf clan, the affidavit provides no additional evidence which would allow the RAD to confirm his identity as a Somali national.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the affidavit does not confirm Somali nationality; appellant could be Somali heritage born elsewhere.

propositions.text: Teacher's letter lacks documentation, is not sworn or notarized, and lacks school letterhead or corroboration
propositions.quote: The RAD has reviewed the letter and notes there is no documentation contained in the submission to ascertain the origin of this letter. The RAD notes the copy is not a sworn affidavit, nor is it notarized. The RAD further notes as much as the author of the letter states he is a teacher from a XXXX XXXX in Qoryoley, there is no supporting documentation to ascertain this statement. The RAD also notes the document is not produced on any form of school letterhead.

propositions.text: Appellant testified he attended school sporadically for four years, last in 2004
propositions.quote: The RAD further notes that the Appellant's testimony was that he attended school sporadically for a total of four years, the last time being in 2004.

propositions.text: Reasonable to expect teacher to produce letter on letterhead or corroborate identity
propositions.quote: The RAD finds it reasonable to expect that an individual who states he is a teacher from a XXXX XXXX would produce his letter on school letterhead or in the least, provide some form of corroborating documentation.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the teacher's letter lacks documentation, is not sworn, and lacks corroboration; appellant testified sporadic schooling.

propositions.text: Teacher's letter statements based on second or third hand information from appellant or family
propositions.quote: The RAD further finds the author makes a series of statements about the incidents associated with the Appellant that consist of knowledge he has gained through reporting from the Appellant or his family members. The author speaks of attending the Appellant's father's burial and speaking to two relatives from whom he obtained much of the information which he relates in the letter. The RAD notes the author in his letter does not confirm speaking with or seeing the Appellant on the day of the burial.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the teacher's letter is based on second or third hand information from the appellant or family.

propositions.text: RAD cannot substantiate identity or provenance of teacher's letter and places little evidentiary weight on it
propositions.quote: The RAD finds it is unable to substantiate the identity of the writer of the document or its provenance. In considering the concerns the RAD has identified and assessing the information it provides, the RAD places little evidentiary weight on the contents of the letter.

propositions.text: If weight placed, letter only places appellant in Somalia in 2004 and does not confirm Somali nationality
propositions.quote: If the RAD were to place any weight on this letter, the RAD finds it simply places the Appellant in Somalia in the year 2004. The RAD further finds this letter cannot be relied upon to substantiate the Appellant's identity as a national of Somalia.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD cannot verify the teacher's letter and gives it little weight; it only places appellant in Somalia in 2004, not confirming nationality.

propositions.text: Letter from friend in South Africa is not original, not sworn or notarized, origin and author unconfirmed, little evidentiary weight
propositions.quote: The RAD notes the letter is not original, but the Appellant submits it is a copy of a document derived from an e-mail. The RAD notes there is no documentation contained in the submission to ascertain the origin of this letter. The RAD further notes the copy is not a sworn affidavit, nor is it notarized. The RAD is unable to confirm the identity of the author or the provenance of the document. The RAD places little evidentiary weight on this document.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the letter from the appellant's friend in South Africa is unverified and gives it little evidentiary weight.

propositions.text: Original marriage certificate submitted under Rule 29(2) application and addressed later
propositions.quote: The original marriage certificate was submitted under a Rule 29(2) Application and the document is addressed in the following section.

paragraphs.summary: The original marriage certificate was submitted under Rule 29(2) and will be addressed later.

propositions.text: Appellant applies under Rule 29(2) to submit documents showing work and marriage in Ethiopia to refute RPD credibility findings
propositions.quote: In his application, the Appellant submits documents which he argues provide evidence that the Appellant was working and that he was married in Ethiopia and that this refutes the credibility findings in respect of his time in Ethiopia at the RPD hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant applies under Rule 29(2) to submit documents showing work and marriage in Ethiopia to refute RPD credibility findings.

propositions.text: Appellant submitted an original marriage certificate dated 2010 and a copy of a letter from 2015 about work in Ethiopia in 2010.
propositions.quote: The Appellant has submitted the following documents with his application: a) An original marriage certificate8 dated XXXX XXXX, 2010. b) A copy of a letter printed from an email dated June 1, 2015, which indicates that the Appellant was working two days per week for four months in 2010 in Ethiopia.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant submitted a 2010 marriage certificate and a 2015 letter about work in Ethiopia in 2010.

propositions.text: RAD must consider document relevance, new evidence, and whether it could have been provided earlier under Rule 29(4).
propositions.quote: Section 29(4) of the RAD Rules states that: 4.) In deciding whether to allow an application, the Division must consider any relevant factors, including a) the document's relevance and probative value; b) any new evidence the document brings to the appeal; and c) whether the person who is the subject of the appeal, with reasonable effort, could have provided the document or written submissions with the appellant's record, respondent's record or reply record.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD must consider document relevance, new evidence, and timing under Rule 29(4).

propositions.text: The original marriage certificate is admissible as additional evidence since a copy was previously submitted.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds this document is admissible as additional evidence in this appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the original marriage certificate admissible as additional evidence.

propositions.text: The copy of the letter from Ethiopia is admitted as additional evidence to confirm aspects of the appellant's testimony.
propositions.quote: The RAD will admit the copy of the letter as additional evidence in this appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD admits the letter from Ethiopia as additional evidence to confirm testimony.

propositions.text: Appellant testified to a religious marriage in Ethiopia in 2010 without a civil record.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes the Appellant testified that he was married in Ethiopia in the summer of 2010 in a "religious ceremony", stating that he could not afford a formal wedding with a reception.

propositions.text: The marriage certificate date contradicts appellant's testimony, raising credibility concerns.
propositions.quote: The RAD further notes the document states the marriage took place on XXXX XXXX, 2010, leading the RAD to question the credibility of the Appellant's testimony in this issue.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant testified to a religious marriage without civil record; the certificate date contradicts this, raising credibility concerns.

propositions.text: The marriage certificate appears to be produced on embossed paper but lacks security features and shows printing flaws.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes the document has been produced without any security features. The RAD further notes when examining the print on this document there appears to be additional print or shadowing of another font in the background indicating this document may have been reprinted at some point in the production process.

propositions.text: It is reasonable to believe Ethiopian authorities would not issue an official document with visible printing flaws.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds it reasonable to believe that the authorities in Ethiopia would not issue an official document with visible printing flaws.

paragraphs.summary: The marriage certificate lacks security features and shows printing flaws unlikely from Ethiopian authorities.

propositions.text: Ink stamps on the document are undermined by signatures written over them, reducing credibility.
propositions.quote: The presence of data written over a seal undermines the integrity of the stamp and as a result, the credibility of the document itself.

paragraphs.summary: Signatures written over ink stamps undermine the document's credibility.

propositions.text: No samples of such documents exist for comparison in IRB records.
propositions.quote: As well the RAD notes no samples of these documents are available in the IRB national documentation country documents for comparison to valid original documents.

propositions.text: Appellant has demonstrated willingness to use fraudulent documents during travel through multiple countries.
propositions.quote: The RAD further notes the Appellant through his oral testimony in respect of his travel through multiple countries has demonstrated he is not adverse to obtaining and utilizing fraudulent documents.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence confirms fraudulent documents are readily available to Somali refugee claimants.
propositions.quote: Further to this, the RAD notes the documentary evidence9 confirms that fraudulent documents are readily available to refugee claimants from Somalia.

paragraphs.summary: No document samples exist; appellant has used fraudulent documents; such documents are readily available to Somali claimants.

propositions.text: The claimant has means and ability to secure fraudulent documents to support refugee claim.
propositions.quote: The RAD is led to conclude the claimant has the means and ability to secure duplicitous documentation to assist in his quest for refugee protection in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD concludes the claimant can obtain fraudulent documents to support his refugee claim.

propositions.text: Documents with authenticity doubts may be given little or no weight without expert verification.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes that where there is sufficient evidence to cast doubt on a document's authenticity, whether because of an irregularity on its face or the questionable circumstances in which it was obtained or provided, a document may be assigned little (or no) weight, without expert verification or where such verification is inconclusive.

propositions.text: Submitting false or irregular documents can affect weight of other documents and overall claimant credibility.
propositions.quote: The RAD also notes that submitting a false or irregular document may have an impact on the weight assigned to other documents provided by the claimant, especially when they are interrelated, and on the overall credibility of a claimant.

paragraphs.summary: Doubtful documents may be given little weight; false documents affect other evidence and claimant credibility.

propositions.text: The marriage certificate is given little evidentiary weight and undermines appellant's credibility on marriage, Ethiopia presence, and persecution claims.
propositions.quote: The panel places little evidentiary weight on the marriage certificate presented as support in this claim. The RAD further finds that this finding severely undermines the credibility of the Appellant in respect of his testimony about his marriage, his presence in Ethiopia and his allegations of persecution in Somalia.

paragraphs.summary: The marriage certificate is given little weight and severely undermines appellant's credibility on key issues.

propositions.text: Appellant submitted a letter from a co-worker in Ethiopia about employment in 2010, but it is not original and lacks verification.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes it is not an original document and the accompanying document indicates it was attached to an e-mail. The RAD further notes the e-mail address does not identify any association with the author of the letter.

propositions.text: The letter is not sworn or notarized; author is unidentified and origin unverifiable.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes the document is not a sworn or notarized affidavit. The RAD has no means to identify the author or verify the origin of the document.

propositions.text: The letter does not specify months of employment and contains unclear statements about the author's knowledge.
propositions.quote: The RAD additionally notes the document does not specify the actual months the Appellant was employed in the year 2010. The RAD has also considered the author of the letter states he was in Dirdawa when the Appellant left Ethiopia. The RAD notes he does not identify the date of this occurrence or how he came to be aware of the information.

propositions.text: The letter's statement conflicts with appellant's BoC document about leaving Ethiopia in April 2011.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds this statement makes little sense considering the Appellant has stated in his BoC document13 that he left Ethiopia in April 2011, a considerable time after allegedly being employed at the XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The letter from co-worker is not original, unverifiable, vague, and conflicts with appellant's own statements.

propositions.text: RPD confronted appellant about residency inconsistencies between BoC and immigration forms.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes the audio recording of the hearing indicates the Appellant was confronted by the RPD at the hearing in respect of statements made in his BoC document, which identified that he resided in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia from December 2009 until April 2011. The RPD at the hearing and in its Reasons noted there was no mention of this in any of his immigration forms completed through his refugee claim process of residing in Dirdawa, Ethiopia.

propositions.text: Appellant testified he did not list all residences but gave no good reason for omissions.
propositions.quote: The Appellant testified that he did not list all of the locations where he lived while there, but offered no salient explanation as to why he chose not to provide accurate residency information to the Immigration and Refugee Board in respect of this eighteen month period of residency in Ethiopia.

paragraphs.summary: RPD confronted appellant about residency inconsistencies; appellant gave no good explanation for omissions.

propositions.text: RAD places little evidentiary weight on the letter due to credibility issues and appellant's testimony.
propositions.quote: The RAD in assessing the credibility issues surrounding the issuing of the letter as well as its contents and considering the Appellant's testimony and documentation of his sojourn in Ethiopia, places little evidentiary weight on the letter.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD gives little evidentiary weight to the letter due to credibility concerns.

propositions.text: Neither the marriage certificate nor the letter sufficiently confirm appellant's residence in Ethiopia after December 2009.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds that neither of the two documents submitted are sufficient to confirm the Appellant's statements that he resided in Ethiopia following his alleged departure from Somalia in December 2009.

paragraphs.summary: Neither document sufficiently confirms appellant's residence in Ethiopia after December 2009.

propositions.text: Counsel made submissions on RAD's role in reviewing RPD decisions.
propositions.quote: Counsel has made submissions in regard to the role that the RAD plays in the review of an RPD decision.

propositions.text: Huruglica decision requires RAD to conduct a hybrid appeal and independently assess refugee status, substituting its own decision if differing from RPD.
propositions.quote: Justice Phelan states in paragraphs 54 and 55 of the foregoing decision: [54] Having concluded that the RAD erred in reviewing the RPD's decision on the standard of reasonableness, I have further concluded that for the reasons above, the RAD is required to conduct a hybrid appeal. It must review all aspects of the RPD's decision and come to an independent assessment of whether the claimant is a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection. Where its assessment departs from that of the RPD, the RAD must substitute its own decision.

propositions.text: RAD can respect RPD credibility findings but is not restricted to intervening only on overriding errors.
propositions.quote: [55] In conducting its assessment, it can recognize and respect the conclusion of the RPD on such issues as credibility and/or where the RPD enjoys a particular advantage in reaching such a conclusion but it is not restricted, as an appellate court is, to intervening on facts only where there is an "overriding and palpable error".

paragraphs.summary: Counsel submitted on RAD's role; Huruglica requires RAD to independently assess and substitute decisions if differing from RPD.

propositions.text: Federal Court allows RAD to apply either standard of review until final judgment settles scope of appellate review.
propositions.quote: Justice Martineau in Alyafi15 has said that, in the face of this conflict, the Federal Court should allow the RAD to apply either approach as long as the question of the scope of the appellate review of the RPD's decisions has not been settled by a final judgment by the Federal Court of Appeal or the Supreme Court of Canada.

paragraphs.summary: Federal Court allows RAD to apply either standard of review until final judgment settles appellate review scope.

propositions.text: RAD will conduct its own assessment and afford deference to RPD credibility findings where appropriate.
propositions.quote: Accordingly, the RAD will conduct its own assessment of the RPD's decision and come to an independent assessment of whether the Appellant is a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection. Deference will be afforded to the credibility findings of the RPD or to other findings where the RPD has a particular advantage in reaching its conclusions.

paragraphs.summary: RAD will independently assess RPD decision, deferring to RPD credibility findings where appropriate.

propositions.text: Appellant argues RPD presumed Article 1E applies and shifted burden to him to disprove it.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits this amounts to unsubstantiated speculation and that the RPD has presumed that Article 1E applies automatically and it is up to the Appellant to prove otherwise.

propositions.text: RAD is not persuaded by appellant's argument about RPD presuming Article 1E applies.
propositions.quote: The RAD is not persuaded by this argument.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant argues RPD presumed Article 1E applies; RAD rejects this argument.

propositions.text: RPD based findings on claimant's testimony and documents, not presuming Article 1E applies or requiring appellant to disprove it.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds the Appellant has taken the statements of the RPD out of context. At no point in reviewing the audio recording of the hearing or its Reasons does the RAD find that the RPD stated or implied that exclusion under Article 1E is being considered as an issue in the claim or that it was necessary for the Appellant to prove that he had not acquired status in other countries.

paragraphs.summary: RPD based findings on evidence and did not presume Article 1E or require appellant to disprove it.

propositions.text: The RPD erred in impugning his credibility about his identity due to inability to corroborate travel testimony.
propositions.quote: The Appellant further submits the RPD has erred in impugning his credibility as to his identity because he could not corroborate his testimony about the countries he had travelled through in order to get to Canada.

propositions.text: The Appellant's own evidence and testimony raised credibility concerns about his travel to Canada, especially his time in Ethiopia.
propositions.quote: The RAD has reviewed the record and finds the Appellant's own evidence and sworn testimony raised the credibility concerns surrounding his travel to Canada.

propositions.text: The Appellant's response to RPD questioning about travel details was designed to minimize the issue but did not address the question.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds his response was designed to minimize the importance of the issue, but it notes he did not address the question as put to him.

propositions.text: The Appellant's response detracts from his ability to act as a credible witness.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds the Appellant's response detracts from his ability to act as a credible witness.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues RPD erred on credibility about travel; the RAD finds his own testimony raised concerns and his responses were evasive, harming credibility.

propositions.text: The Appellant gave contradictory testimony about family location and ties to Ethiopia to US authorities.
propositions.quote: The RAD further notes the Appellant provided contradictory testimony about the location of his family members and his ties to Ethiopia to US authorities.

propositions.text: The Appellant gave inconsistent testimony about travel to Canada compared to his BoC and other documents.
propositions.quote: In addition he provided inconsistent testimony in respect of his travel to Canada when compared to his BoC and other documents.

propositions.text: It is reasonable to expect the Appellant to have documentation of residency given his extended time in various countries.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds it reasonable to believe that the Appellant having resided for an extended time in countries where he worked and interacted with various individuals would provide some form of documentation of his residency there.

propositions.text: The Appellant's evidence raised possibility of potential status in other locations.
propositions.quote: The RAD having reviewed the record finds the Appellant's own evidence raised the possibility of potential status in other locations.

propositions.text: The RPD ignored the Appellant's sworn testimony about travel, violating principles in Maldonado.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that the RPD ignored the Appellant's sworn testimony in respect of his travel and in doing so violates the principles set out in Maldonado.

propositions.text: Maldonado states sworn allegations create a presumption of truth unless there is reason to doubt them.
propositions.quote: When an applicant swears to the truth of certain allegations, this creates a presumption that those allegations are true unless there be reason to doubt their truthfulness.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds contradictory and inconsistent testimony undermines credibility; the appellant argues RPD ignored sworn testimony per Maldonado, which presumes truth absent doubt.

propositions.text: Concerns about the Appellant's credibility negate the presumption of truthfulness of his sworn testimony.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds that concerns surrounding the Appellant's credibility negate the presumption of truthfulness associated with the Appellant's sworn testimony.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds credibility concerns negate the presumption of truthfulness of the appellant's sworn testimony.

propositions.text: It was proper for the RPD to explore credibility issues in its determination.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds it was well within the purview of the RPD to explore these issues in arriving at its determination in this claim.

propositions.text: The RAD agrees with the RPD's conclusion and rejects the Appellant's argument.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds it agrees with the conclusion of the RPD and the Appellant's argument must fail.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds RPD properly explored credibility issues and agrees with RPD's conclusion, rejecting appellant's argument.

propositions.text: The RPD found the Appellant's identity witnesses failed to establish his Somali nationality.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the Appellant's identity witnesses were unable to establish that the Appellant is a national of Somalia.

propositions.text: The RPD's reasons for discounting Mr. XXXX's evidence are inadequate; total evidence establishes identity.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits that the RPD reasons for discounting the evidence of Mr. XXXX are inadequate. The Appellant further submits that the totality of the evidence of both witnesses establishes the Appellant's personal and national identity.

propositions.text: The RAD is not persuaded by the Appellant's argument about identity witnesses.
propositions.quote: The RAD is not persuaded by this argument.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found identity witnesses failed to establish Somali nationality; appellant argues otherwise; RAD is not persuaded.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX alleges relation to Appellant but his testimony on identity was vague and lacked credibility.
propositions.quote: The RAD in reviewing the audio recording of the hearing notes the first witness Mr. XXXX alleges he is related to the Appellant, but his testimony in respect of establishing the identity of the Appellant was vague and lacking in credibility.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX left Somalia in 1990 when Appellant was about three years old.
propositions.quote: The witness testified that he left Somalia in 1990 (the Appellant would have been approximately three years old).

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX discussed the Appellant and his presence in Canada with the Appellant's mother before meeting him in Canada.
propositions.quote: He testified that he had discussions about the Appellant and his presence in Canada with the Appellant's mother, prior to encountering the Appellant in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds Mr. XXXX's testimony vague and not credible; he left Somalia in 1990 and discussed the Appellant with his mother before meeting him.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX's responses about discussions with Appellant were vague, hesitant, and lacked specific detail.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds the responses of the witness lacked specific detail and was hesitant.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX said they discussed 'who the target was at home' and 'people with different religious beliefs' but gave no further detail.
propositions.quote: For example he stated they discussed, "who the target was at home"...He replied, "People with different religious beliefs".

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX said they did not discuss why Appellant left Somalia in depth.
propositions.quote: He was asked if he and the Appellant discussed why he left Somalia. He responded, "No we did not go as deeply as that".

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX knew very little personal information about the Appellant, including mother's full name, religion, or marital status.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes the witness was aware of very little personal information about the Appellant. For example he was unaware of the Appellant's mother's full name, what the Appellant's religious affiliation was or whether he was married.

paragraphs.summary: Mr. XXXX's testimony was vague and hesitant, lacking detail about discussions and personal information about the Appellant.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX gave vague, non-specific answers about why Appellant left Somalia and about Appellant's father.
propositions.quote: He replied, "No, but I know why"..."He is from the group that spreads religion and they don't like that"...he stated that the Appellant's mother told him.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX was non-responsive and required repeated questioning about Appellant's father's status.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes the witness was non-responsive and the question was put to him three times before he responded indicating his father was dead.

paragraphs.summary: Mr. XXXX gave vague answers about why Appellant left Somalia and was non-responsive about Appellant's father, needing repeated questioning.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXX provided no persuasive evidence of relation to Appellant and his testimony lacked credibility.
propositions.quote: The RAD in reviewing the record finds that Mr. XXXX provided no persuasive evidence to support that he was related to the Appellant. Further to this the RAD finds Mr. XXXX testimony was lacking in credibility.

propositions.text: Information Mr. XXXX had about Appellant's identity could have been acquired from others.
propositions.quote: Additionally the RAD finds, on a balance of probabilities, that any information that he had acquired in reference to the Appellant's identity and circumstances in Somalia could have been acquired in conversation with others.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds Mr. XXXX's testimony not credible and any information he had could have come from others, not personal knowledge.

propositions.text: Second identity witness Mr. XXXX's testimony was vague and lacked specific detail.
propositions.quote: In respect of the second identity witness, Mr. XXXX, the RAD in reviewing the audio recording of his exchange with the RPD notes his testimony was also vague and lacking in specific detail.

propositions.text: Appellant testified he and second witness spoke daily since meeting in Canada.
propositions.quote: The Appellant testified that he and the witness spoke every day since meeting in Canada.

propositions.text: Appellant's responses about time and topics of conversations with second witness were vague and evasive.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds the Appellant's responses to this inquiry were vague and evasive.

propositions.text: Both Appellant and second witness related encounters in Somalia in 2005 and 2009.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes that both the Appellant and the witness were able to relate an encounter with the Appellant in Somalia in the year 2005. The witness then noted that he saw the Appellant again in 2009 in Somalia.

propositions.text: Second witness provided few personal details about Appellant's family or youth beyond shared soccer interest.
propositions.quote: The RAD additionally notes Mr. XXXX was able to provide few personal details about the Appellant's family or the Appellant when they were young, beyond a common interest in soccer.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds second witness's testimony vague; appellant's responses about conversations were evasive; they met in Somalia and shared little personal detail.

propositions.text: Second witness's responses about discussions with Appellant in Canada were hesitant, evasive, and required prompting.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds his responses were hesitant and at times evasive, often requiring prompting from the RPD.

propositions.text: Second witness and Appellant gave different ages when they met; witness said Somali people don't discuss tribe and age.
propositions.quote: The RPD asked the witness about his age when he met the Appellant and his answer and the Appellant's answer were not the same. When he was asked to explain why, he answered, "Somali people don't discuss tribe and age".

propositions.text: Appellant's responses about distinctive features of their Somali town were hesitant and vague.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds the Appellant's responses when questioned about distinctive features about the town in which he and the Appellant lived in Somalia were equally hesitant and vague.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds second witness's answers hesitant and evasive; age answers differed; appellant's responses about Somali town were vague.

propositions.text: Second witness and Appellant encountered each other in Somalia and shared soccer interest but little else.
propositions.quote: The RAD, in considering the testimony of the witness finds that the witness and the Appellant had indeed encountered each other in Somalia and shared common interest in soccer, but little more.

propositions.text: Witness provided some info about Appellant's father and Al-Shabab but little else about family.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes it was of interest that the witness was able to relate information about the Appellant's father and the problems with Al-Shabab despite being able to provide limited information about the Appellant's family beyond this issue.

propositions.text: Vague testimony about Canada discussions could have been provided by Appellant himself.
propositions.quote: The RAD, in considering the vague and evasive testimony provided by the Appellant and Mr. XXXX in reference to their discussions in Canada, finds this information could have been provided by the Appellant in the course of the Canadian conversations.

propositions.text: RAD places little weight on testimony about Appellant's father and finds witness did not confirm Appellant's Somali nationality.
propositions.quote: The RAD places little weight on the testimony about the Appellant's father. The RAD further finds Mr. XXXX did not provide persuasive testimony to confirm the Appellant's identity as a national of Somalia.

propositions.text: RAD agrees with RPD's finding on identity witnesses after review.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds upon its review of the testimony of the identity witnesses it agrees with the finding of the RPD.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds second witness and appellant met in Somalia but shared little; testimony about father is weak; RAD agrees with RPD's negative finding on identity witnesses.

propositions.text: RPD failed to consider other evidence supporting Appellant's identity, including US claim documents and letters.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits that the RPD failed to have regard for other forms of evidence submitted in support of his identity.

propositions.text: RPD considered all evidence but only referenced evidence relevant to its decision in Reasons.
propositions.quote: The RAD in reviewing the Reasons from this claim finds the RPD does state that it considered all of the evidence, but it only refers to the evidence in its Reasons that is relevant to its decision.

propositions.text: RAD is not persuaded by Appellant's argument about other identity evidence.
propositions.quote: The RAD is not persuaded by the argument of the Appellant.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues RPD ignored other identity evidence; RAD finds RPD considered all evidence and is not persuaded by appellant's argument.

propositions.text: RAD independently reviewed and assessed the documents and hearing audio recording.
propositions.quote: The RAD has independently reviewed and assessed these documents as well as the audio recording of the hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD independently reviewed the documents and hearing audio recording.

propositions.text: Appellant stated to US authorities he held a legally issued Somali passport but later said it was from a smuggler with only his picture.
propositions.quote: In respect of the Appellant's US claim documents, the Appellant in his interview with US authorities stated that he held a legally issued Somali passport. Yet when confronted by the RPD about these statements he stated that the document was a Somali passport obtained from the smuggler and it only contained his picture.

propositions.text: Appellant's sworn statement in US proceedings lacked credibility and no genuine documents were provided to US authorities.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds the Appellant's testimony provided in his Record of Sworn Statement in Proceedings document, was lacking in credibility. The RAD in reviewing this document finds no persuasive evidence that the Appellant provided any genuine documents to US authorities in order to establish his identity.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds appellant's US passport claim inconsistent and his sworn statement lacks credibility; no genuine documents were provided to US authorities.

propositions.text: Letter from Somali Center of Kansas City states two individuals were aware of facts but does not explain how they knew.
propositions.quote: The RAD on reviewing this document notes the document from the SCKCM states the two individuals listed in the document stated to the author of the letter that they were aware of the facts stated therein. The RAD finds the letter does not indicate how these individuals came to be aware of this information.

propositions.text: RAD places little weight on this letter as proof of Appellant's identity.
propositions.quote: The RAD places little weight on this document as proof of the Appellant's identity.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the SCKCM letter lacks explanation of source and places little weight on it as proof of identity.

propositions.text: Letter from Somali Immigrant Aid Organization is based on self-reported interview and author's opinion, not documented fact.
propositions.quote: The RAD on reviewing this document notes it is based on a self-reported interview with the Appellant and the author's observations from the interview. The RAD finds this letter is not founded in any documented fact, but it is simply the author's opinion about the Appellant.

propositions.text: RAD places little evidentiary weight on this letter for establishing Appellant's identity.
propositions.quote: The RAD places little evidentiary weight on this document in establishing the identity of the Appellant.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the SIAO letter is opinion-based and places little evidentiary weight on it for identity.

propositions.text: Affidavit from Appellant's mother confirms his name but does not establish Somali nationality.
propositions.quote: The RAD reviewed the affidavit from the Appellant's mother and notes it states the Appellant is her son and that his father was killed in Somalia. The RAD finds the document confirms the Appellant's name, but it does not serve to establish his identity as a national of Somalia.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the mother's affidavit confirms the appellant's name but not his Somali nationality.

propositions.text: Additional documents submitted provide no persuasive support for Appellant's Somali nationality.
propositions.quote: The RAD has reviewed the Appellant's additional documents submitted in support of his identity and finds they provide no additional persuasive support in establishing the Appellant's identity as a national of Somalia.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds additional documents do not persuasively establish the appellant's Somali nationality.

propositions.text: RPD found Appellant's testimony about reasons for leaving Somalia inconsistent between US and Canadian claims, undermining credibility.
propositions.quote: The RPD found the Appellant's testimony as to the reasons he left Somalia were inconsistent in respect of the information provided in his US and Canadian refugee claims and this undermines his ability to act as a credible witness.

propositions.text: Appellant submits he provided a reasonable explanation to the RPD about inconsistencies.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits he provided a reasonable explanation to the RPD.

propositions.text: RAD is not persuaded by the Appellant's argument about his explanation.
propositions.quote: The RAD is not persuaded by the argument of the Appellant.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found inconsistencies in appellant's reasons for leaving Somalia; appellant says he explained reasonably; RAD is not persuaded.

propositions.text: The RAD notes the Appellant was confronted by the RPD about inconsistency in his statements to US authorities about his father's death.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes the Appellant was confronted by the RPD at the first sitting of his claim about the inconsistency in his statements to US authorities as to how his father was killed in Somalia.

propositions.text: The RPD explained the US statement did not mention Al-Shabab but said local people killed his father over a farm dispute.
propositions.quote: The RPD explained to the claimant that his testimony in the US Record of Sworn Statement in Proceedings document22 does not mention the words Al-Shabab anywhere. The RPD further noted that the US document stated that his father was killed by "local people who were fighting over a farm his father owned".

propositions.text: The Appellant said he told US authorities 'local people' meant Al-Shabab, but RAD finds 'local people' does not link to Al-Shabab.
propositions.quote: The Appellant replied stating, "I did (tell them) when I said they are local people". The RAD does not find the description "local people" provides any linkage to Al-Shabab.

propositions.text: The Appellant later changed testimony to say a man from Mogadishu claimed his father's farm and killed him, but RAD finds no indication this man was a 'local person'.
propositions.quote: He later modified his testimony to state, "A man who came from Mogadishu...claimed my father's farm was his and they got in a fight and they killed my father". The RAD finds the Appellant's later testimony does not indicate that this individual is a "local person".

paragraphs.summary: The RAD notes the Appellant was confronted by the RPD about inconsistent statements on his father's death, finds 'local people' does not link to Al-Shabab, and his later testimony lacks clarity.

propositions.text: The RAD notes the Appellant denied any interaction with Al-Shabab and recruitment attempts during US questioning.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes the Appellant was questioned directly by the US authorities about Al-Shabab and he denied any interaction with them. The Appellant answered in the negative when asked by US authorities if any terrorist organization had attempted to recruit him.

propositions.text: The RPD asked if the Appellant feared Al-Shabab during his US claim; he hesitated but eventually said yes.
propositions.quote: The RPD asked the Appellant if at the time he made his US asylum claim if he was afraid of Al-Shabab. He hesitated and eventually answered, "Yes".

propositions.text: The RPD noted the Appellant did not mention Al-Shabab in US testimony and was evasive when asked to explain why.
propositions.quote: The RPD noted for the Appellant that he did not mention Al-Shabab at any point in his US testimony and asked him to explain why. The Appellant was evasive and attempted to avoid providing a response.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD notes the Appellant denied Al-Shabab interaction in US questioning, hesitated about fearing them, and was evasive about not mentioning them.

propositions.text: At second sitting, Appellant said he was told by Somalis not to mention Al-Shabab or face deportation.
propositions.quote: During the second sitting of his claim, the Appellant during questioning by his counsel was asked why did not mention Al-Shabab in his US Record of Sworn Statement in Proceedings interview. He answered, "I was told by other Somalis not to mention Al-Shabab or I would be deported".

propositions.text: RAD finds it reasonable that if true, Appellant would have said this at first sitting when questioned twice about it.
propositions.quote: The RAD further finds it is reasonable to believe if this was the situation the Appellant would have provided this testimony during the first sitting of his claim during the two occasions he was questioned about it.

propositions.text: The Federal Court says a person's first story is usually most genuine and most believable, but failure to report a fact depends on circumstances.
propositions.quote: A person's first story is usually the most genuine and, therefore, the one to be most believed. That being said, although the failure to report a fact can be a cause for concern, it should not always be so. That, again depends on all the circumstances: see Fajardo v. Canada (Minister of Employment and Immigration), [1993] F.C.J. No. 915 at para. 5 (QL) (C.A.); Owusu-Ansah, supra; and Sheikh v. Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration), [2000] F.C.J. No. 568 (QL) (T.D.).23

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the Appellant's claim he was told not to mention Al-Shabab is not credible as he did not say so earlier; cites Federal Court on first story credibility.

propositions.text: The RAD finds the Appellant consciously chose not to provide his latter testimony at first sitting despite multiple opportunities.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes the Appellant was given multiple opportunities to provide his latter testimony during the first sitting of his claim and he consciously chose not to do so.

propositions.text: The Appellant's testimony evolved to offset previous inconsistencies, lacking credibility and undermining his refugee claim.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds the Appellant's testimony on this issue evolved throughout his RPD hearing. The RAD finds the Appellant's evolving testimony was an attempt to offset his previous inconsistent testimony. The RAD finds the Appellant's latter explanation is lacking in credibility and undermines the basis of his claim for refugee protection.

propositions.text: The RAD agrees with the RPD's finding on this issue and rejects the Appellant's argument.
propositions.quote: The RAD agrees with the finding of the RPD in this area. The Appellant's argument must fail.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the Appellant's evolving testimony lacks credibility, agrees with RPD, and rejects the Appellant's argument.

propositions.text: The Appellant submits the RPD made negative credibility findings based on microscopic examination of minor issues.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits that the RPD engaged in a series of negative credibility findings based on microscopic examination.

propositions.text: The Appellant submits these issues are minor and not material to core claim issues.
propositions.quote: The Appellant further submits that these issues are minor in nature and are not material to the core issues of the claim.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues the RPD's negative credibility findings are minor and not material to core claim issues.

propositions.text: The Appellant testified he married in Ethiopia in 2010 and US authorities mistakenly called his wife a fiancée.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits that he testified during the RPD hearing that he was married in the summer of 2010 in Ethiopia. The Appellant further testified that the US authorities made a mistake in identifying this wife as his fiancée.

propositions.text: The Appellant submits the RPD used his failure to provide supporting documents to impugn his credibility.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits that the RPD has used the Appellant's failure to supply supporting documentation in his claim as a method of impugning the Appellant's credibility.

propositions.text: The RAD notes the Appellant submitted the original marriage license as new evidence and has addressed credibility concerns about it.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes the Appellant submitted the original marriage license as new evidence in this appeal as support for his identity and his presence in Ethiopia. The RAD has previously addressed credibility concerns associated with the authenticity of this document.

propositions.text: The RAD finds the Appellant's testimony that US authorities made a mistake is not credible.
propositions.quote: The RAD in considering the finding associated with the marriage certificate further finds that the Appellant's testimony that the US authorities made a mistake is not credible.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant says he married in Ethiopia and US authorities erred; RAD finds his testimony about US mistake not credible.

propositions.text: The RPD found the Appellant's testimony about his family's location inconsistent between US and Canadian claims, undermining credibility.
propositions.quote: The RPD found the Appellant's testimony regarding the location of his family was inconsistent in respect of the information provided in his US and Canadian refugee claims and this further undermines his ability to act as a credible witness.

propositions.text: The Appellant submits the US translator made a mistake and the RPD relied microscopically on US interview notes.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits that the US translator made a mistake in his US testimony. The Appellant further submits that this is a minor error and the RPD microscopically relied on the US interview notes.

propositions.text: The RAD is not persuaded by the RPD's findings on this issue.
propositions.quote: The RAD is not persuaded by the findings of the RPD on this issue.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found family location testimony inconsistent; Appellant blames US translator; RAD is not persuaded by RPD's findings.

propositions.text: The RAD reviewed the audio and notes the US interview document had multiple inconsistencies.
propositions.quote: The RAD has reviewed the audio recording of the hearing and notes the Appellant's US interview document was the source of multiple inconsistencies such as this.

propositions.text: The Appellant acknowledged many 'mistakes' in his US Record of Sworn Statement in Proceedings interview.
propositions.quote: The RAD further notes that in its review of the Appellant's testimony in respect of the Appellant's testimony surrounding his US Record of Sworn Statement in Proceedings interview,24 the Appellant acknowledged there were many "mistakes".

propositions.text: The Appellant blamed inconsistencies on US authorities when confronted by the RPD.
propositions.quote: The Appellant was confronted by the RPD during his testimony at various points and asked to explain these inconsistencies. In every circumstance, the Appellant blamed the inconsistencies on mistakes made by the US authorities.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD notes multiple inconsistencies in US interview document; Appellant admitted mistakes and blamed US authorities.

propositions.text: The Appellant was asked if he wanted to add information to US interview and signed a declaration confirming its truth.
propositions.quote: The RAD has examined the document and notes the Appellant was asked if there was any additional information in the US interview that he cared to add. The Appellant also signed a declaration stating that he read the document following the interview, acknowledging that the contents were true and correct.

propositions.text: The Appellant had multiple opportunities to amend his documents at the RPD hearing if aware of inconsistencies.
propositions.quote: The RAD further notes that the Appellant at the outset of his hearing before the RPD was provided with an opportunity to amend his documents. The RAD finds if the Appellant was aware of inconsistencies in this document he was given multiple opportunities to correct the information.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant signed US interview document as true and had multiple chances to amend inconsistencies at RPD hearing.

propositions.text: The RAD finds the Appellant's claim that US immigration interview was inaccurate lacks credibility.
propositions.quote: Additionally the RAD finds the Appellant's statement that his interview with US immigration officials was not accurate lacks credibility.

propositions.text: The US interview was conducted by DOJ officers following protocols; Appellant gave no persuasive evidence to the contrary.
propositions.quote: The interview was conducted by officers of the US Department of Justice, Immigration and Naturalization Service in accordance with specific protocols and the Appellant has adduced no persuasive evidence to indicate they are not acting in accordance with these protocols.

propositions.text: The RAD finds the Appellant's explanation for inconsistencies is not credible.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds the Appellant's explanation for these inconsistencies is not credible.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the Appellant's claim that US interview was inaccurate and his explanation for inconsistencies not credible.

propositions.text: The Appellant testified he omitted employment info from IMM5669 because 'this is not a job'.
propositions.quote: A further example arises when the Appellant is confronted by the RPD about his testimony in respect to his employment in Ethiopia and later in South Africa. The Appellant testified in his Canadian hearing that he did omit the employment information from his IMM5669 document because, "This is not a job".

propositions.text: The Appellant told US authorities about his employment in Ethiopia and South Africa.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes when he was questioned by US authorities about his employment, the Appellant clearly identifies his work in Ethiopia and South Africa.

propositions.text: The RAD finds the Appellant's explanation for omitting employment info is not credible.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds the Appellant's explanation before the RPD in this matter is simply not credible.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant omitted employment info in Canada but disclosed it in US; RAD finds his explanation not credible.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues the employment omission was a minor inconsistency.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that this was a minor inconsistency.

propositions.text: The RAD disagrees; Appellant's travels and presence in countries are key to his refugee claim.
propositions.quote: The RAD disagrees with this argument by the Appellant. The Appellant has alleged he has travelled through these various countries in order to escape persecution in Somalia. The RAD notes that the Appellant spent extended periods of time in a number of countries that are signatories to the UN Convention on Refugees. The RAD finds that the Appellant's presence and activities in these countries are key components of his claim for refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant says employment omission is minor; RAD finds his travels and presence in countries key to claim.

propositions.text: The Appellant confirmed transit through Sudan and Mozambique for two months in US documents but did not mention them in IMM0008 form.
propositions.quote: A further situation arose when the Appellant was questioned about his travels following his departure from Ethiopia. The Appellant confirmed his statements from his US documents that he transited through Sudan and Mozambique for two months. The RPD noted that his IMM0008 form did not mention these two countries as part of his journey to Canada.

propositions.text: The Appellant explained these were 'transit' countries, but RAD finds this explanation makes little sense given time spent there.
propositions.quote: The Appellant's explanation was that these were "transit" countries. The RAD finds this explanation makes little sense when one considers that the Appellant spent more time in these countries than some of the South American countries he listed in his documents.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant said Sudan and Mozambique were transit countries but omitted them in IMM0008; RAD finds explanation illogical.

propositions.text: The Appellant submits the RPD's finding on his family's location is minor and microscopic examination.
propositions.quote: The Appellant further submits that the RPD finding in respect to the actual location of his mother and siblings is a minor issue and amounts to a microscopic examination of the evidence.

propositions.text: The RAD disagrees and finds family location important to identity and credibility assessment.
propositions.quote: The RAD does not agree with the argument of the Appellant. The RAD finds that the current country of residence of the Appellant's family is an important and relevant factor in the assessment of the Appellant's identity as well as the credibility of his allegations.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant says family location finding is minor; RAD finds it important to identity and credibility.

propositions.text: The RAD finds the Appellant's argument that inconsistencies are minor and not material is incorrect.
propositions.quote: The RAD has considered the Appellant's argument that some of these inconsistencies and contradictions when viewed as singular credibility findings could be regarded as not being material to the core issues of the claim. The RAD has reviewed a number of these findings and finds this assessment of the Appellant's testimony and evidence is not microscopic. The RAD finds these concerns are not founded on minor issues, but provide information which is central to the core elements of the claim. The RAD finds the argument of the Appellant must fail.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the Appellant's argument that inconsistencies are minor and immaterial must fail.

propositions.text: Dan-Ash case says witness contradictions can justify rejecting evidence even by generous trier of fact.
propositions.quote: With regard to the credibility of the evidence that the Appellant has submitted, the RAD refers to the sentiment expressed in the case of Dan-Ash that: ... unless one is prepared to postulate (and accept) unlimited credulity on the part of the Board, there must come a point at which a witness's contradictions will move even the most generous trier of fact to reject his evidence.25

paragraphs.summary: The RAD cites Dan-Ash that witness contradictions can justify rejecting evidence even by generous fact-finder.

propositions.text: Sheikh case says a general lack of credibility finding may extend to all relevant testimony information.
propositions.quote: As well the RAD notes in Sheikh,26 MacGuigan, J.A., writing for the court, stated, in part:, "In other words a general finding of a lack of credibility on the part of the applicant may conceivably extend to all relevant information emanating from his testimony."

paragraphs.summary: The RAD cites Sheikh that a general lack of credibility finding may extend to all relevant testimony information.

propositions.text: The RAD finds cumulative credibility issues lead to conclusion the Appellant failed to act as a credible witness.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds when one assesses the cumulative effect of the numerous credibility issues arising from the Appellant's testimony and the accompanying documentation, these findings lead the RAD to conclude the Appellant has failed to act as a credible witness.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds cumulative credibility issues mean the Appellant failed to act as a credible witness.

propositions.text: Section 110(6) allows RAD to hold hearing if documentary evidence raises serious credibility issue central to RPD decision and justifies claim outcome.
propositions.quote: According to Section 110(6), the RAD may hold a hearing if, in its opinion, there is documentary evidence referred to in 110(3) that raises a serious issue with respect to the credibility of the Appellant, that is central to the RPD's decision, and that, if accepted, would justify allowing or rejecting the refugee protection claim.

propositions.text: In this appeal, with no evidence from Minister, documentary evidence in Section 110(3) must be understood with Section 110(4).
propositions.quote: In this appeal, where there is no evidence from or in response to the Minister, the documentary evidence referred to in Section 110(3) must be understood in relation to Section 110(4).

paragraphs.summary: Section 110(6) allows RAD hearing if documentary evidence raises serious credibility issue central to RPD decision; here, evidence must be read with Section 110(4).

propositions.text: Sections 110(3), (4), and (6) together mean RAD must not hold hearing unless new evidence raises serious credibility issue central to RPD decision and justifies claim outcome.
propositions.quote: When read together, Sections 110(3), (4), and (6) establish that the RAD must not hold a hearing in an appeal such as this unless there is new (Section 110(4)) evidence, in which case the RAD may hold a hearing if that new evidence raises a serious issue with respect to the credibility of the Appellant, is central to the RPD's decision, and that, if accepted, would justify allowing or rejecting the refugee protection claim.

paragraphs.summary: Sections 110(3), (4), and (6) require new evidence raising serious credibility issue central to RPD decision to hold RAD hearing.

propositions.text: The Appellant submits no new evidence raising serious credibility issues or central to the RPD's decision to justify allowing or rejecting the claim
propositions.quote: The Appellant has submitted no new evidence in support of his appeal that raises a serious issue with respect to the credibility of the Appellant or that is central to the RPD's decision, and would justify allowing or rejecting the refugee protection claim.

propositions.text: The RAD must proceed without a hearing based on the RPD record and denies the oral hearing application
propositions.quote: As such, the RAD must proceed without a hearing on the basis of the RPD's record, and his application for an oral hearing is denied.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant submits no new evidence raising serious credibility issues or central to the RPD's decision; the RAD denies oral hearing and proceeds on RPD record.

propositions.text: The Appellant failed to act as a credible witness in his refugee protection claim
propositions.quote: The Appellant failed to act as a credible witness in his quest for refugee protection.

propositions.text: The Appellant may have resided in Somalia at some time; last identified there in 2009
propositions.quote: The Appellant may have resided in Somalia at some time during his life. The Appellant was last identified in Somalia in 2009.

propositions.text: The Appellant failed to provide persuasive evidence of Somali or any other nationality
propositions.quote: The Appellant was unable to provide persuasive evidence that he is a national of Somalia or any other country.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the Appellant not credible, possibly lived in Somalia until 2009, but failed to prove Somali or other nationality.

propositions.text: Section 111(1)(a) of IRPA governs confirmation of RPD decisions on refugee status
propositions.quote: Pursuant to Section 111(1)(a) of IRPA, the RAD confirms the decision of the RPD

propositions.text: The RAD confirms the RPD decision that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor in need of protection
propositions.quote: the RAD confirms the decision of the RPD that the Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed accordingly
propositions.quote: Accordingly, this appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD confirms under IRPA s.111(1)(a) the RPD decision denying refugee status and dismisses the appeal.
